query: what is the speed of sound?
answer:
In dry air at 20 °C (68 °F), sound travels at about 343 metres per second [1][2]. That's roughly 1,235 km/h, 1,125 ft/s or 767 mph. Some sources round it to 344 m/s (about 770 mph) [3].

The speed changes mostly with air temperature. A common rule of thumb is c ≈ 331.3 + 0.606 × T m/s, where T is the temperature in °C, so sound is slower in cold air and faster in warm air. Humidity and air pressure make only a small difference [1]. Sound moves faster through liquids and solids, such as water or steel, because it depends on what the material is made of [3].
